rationale: The assistant covered the power checks, spur and consumer unit, and door latch with safe instructions (power off before any fuse swap), and ended by escalating to an engineer when the fuse check can't be done. It said the neon on the spur 'usually' means the fuse is fine, a reasonable hedge. The plug-fuse and plug-hunt advice was repeated across several turns, and it never asked for the door-edge label to get the make or model. It also floated control board costs and the suspects (on/off switch, mains filter) without strong evidence, though it hedged them.
